drop.title: The Last Peg Was Decided Before You Started

title: The Last Peg Was
Decided Before
You Started
slides.dek: Peg solitaire feels like pure trial and error. But two colours you never see, unchanged by every jump, fix the final peg's fate the instant you lift the first one, and leave it just five holes on the whole board.

slides.body: The English board is thirty-three holes in a cross, every one filled but the middle. A move hops a peg over a neighbour into the empty hole beyond, and the hopped peg is removed; keep going until one peg is left. Most people never finish. But here is what almost nobody asks: when you do reach one peg, *where* is it allowed to be? Not anywhere. From the centre start it can end in only *five* holes, the middle and the four arm tips, and that was settled before your first move.

Colour the board by r + c modulo 3, three diagonal stripes. A jump slides a peg two holes in a line, so it touches all three colours once: it empties one, empties its neighbour, fills the third. Read the colours as the non-zero elements of *GF(4)* (1, ω, ω²), where each doubles to zero and all three sum to zero, so that one-of-each cancels. The totals *T* over r + c and *U* over r − c never move. The lone final peg must match the start on both, and those two equations pin it to five holes.

lines.sub: rotate format back to game after four of the last seven ran research. picked peg solitaire and de bruijn's 1972 GF(4) resource count, a cousin of #034's fifteen-puzzle parity invariant but a different algebra, colouring over a finite field

three modules over one board engine: play the english board with a 'watch it solve' 31-jump perfect game; click a hole empty and the two GF(4) labels light every finish still permitted; a 13-hole diamond where permitted and reachable part ways

offline first: the two labels held fixed over 192,118 random legal jumps (0 changes); the centre permits exactly 5 finishes and a DFS reaches all 5, one line landing dead centre; on the 13-hole diamond all 39 reachable positions enumerated, none a lone peg

where the last peg
lands was decided

slides.sub: Play the English board, then press Watch it solve to see a 31-jump line drop the last peg dead centre. Click any hole empty and the two hidden colours, T and U, light every finish still allowed, exactly five from the middle. Then meet the honest twist: a little diamond those colours say can finish, that the board never actually lets you reach.
